newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks set for records, profit-taking may arise.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks set for records, profit-taking may arise.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index is expected to push ahead to a record high on Friday but brokers said profit-taking could set in later with prices, particularly in the property sector, looking overbought in the short term.
"It will probably set another record today," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "In the near term, reaching 16,500 is possible."
The Hang Seng Index surged 382.53 points, or 2.39 percent, to close at a record high of 16,365.71 points on Thursday.
Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index of Hong Kong stocks in London gained 44.88 points to 16,410.59.
"In the short run the market is quite overbought, but this rally is quite strong and it is hard to predict the top," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.

"This bull run is not totally based on fundamentals. It is more liquidity driven so it is not easy to predict where it will go," he said, adding that the Hang Seng Index could test 16,500 points before a pullback towards 16,200.
Mak saw the buying interest boosting property stocks spreading out into second line stocks.
"There might be some profit-taking," he added.
